paper_title: $A'$ view of the sunrise: Boosting helioscopes with angular information
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing epsilon (chi), dimensionless, exactly as plotted on y-axis
notes: Solar dark photon helioscope (not a DM haloscope, so no local DM density). Constrains kinetic mixing epsilon vs DP mass m. Main results are two curves in the m-epsilon plane (Fig. 5/8): 'darks' (optimistic, data-driven background subtraction) and 'eclipse'. No numerical tables for the limit curves are provided; data points here are approximate readings/anchors from Table 1 (sensitivity to epsilon ~1e-9 at m=1 eV for darks, 4e-8 for eclipse) and Fig. 6 benchmark points (m=400 eV eps=6.1e-11, m=15 eV eps=1.2e-10 near exclusion). Points given are for the darks (optimistic) limit; resonant bump enhances sensitivity in 5-300 eV range. Values are approximate. 90% CL. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.68, 33)) | Vision: Figure 5 (fig_00.png) shows this work's constraints in the m-epsilon plane. The lower exclusion boundary is the envelope of the strongest limits: the solid blue 'Eclipse (November 13, 2012)' curve dominates at m < ~0.025 eV (slope ~ -1, epsilon ~ 4e-8/m), and the solid purple 'Darks, data-driven background subtraction' (the most optimistic darks limit, labeled 'HINODE: darks (optimistic)' in Fig 8) dominates at larger masses. Calibrated using Table 1 (fig_03): Eclipse sensitivity 4e-8 and Darks 1e-9 at m=1 eV; kink masses 2e-6 eV (eclipse) and 3e-2 eV (darks). Broad resonant dip reaches ~1.4e-12 near m~50-200 eV, then rises steeply near m~3-5 keV (detector max energy). Y-axis is dimensionless kinetic mixing (epsilon). Confidence limit 90% CL per text.
